Both items filed (I-1346 issue, I-1348 memory). Report follows.

## Verdict

The previous reviewer's conclusion is **substantially right on the mathematics and wrong on the bookkeeping**. Every stated rejection ground still holds against the current Lean tree — I checked each cited declaration and each cited line, and none has rotted. But the conclusion answered "are these refutations correct?" when the question a prover lane asks is "may I attempt this?", and those come apart in two places. Also: the board has **five** rejected leaves, not four, and the parent's own summary both says "four" and rejects the fifth two paragraphs later.

Not churning, not stuck — this cluster is *closed correctly and described stale*. The defect is entirely in forwarding text.

## Per leaf

**joint-cover — REJECTED-AS: false-statement** · cause cited: `FinCoverData` types pieces into the two pinned charts, so relaxing the partition *fields* cannot move where pieces live · cause still holds: **YES** — `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamily.lean:166` (`h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, …V₀)`), `:168` (`h₁` into `V₁`), `:186` `pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen ∘ h₀) (basicOpen ∘ h₁)` — verbatim as cited, and `FinCoverData` is still rooted (`AlgebraicJacobian.lean:342`) · re-openable: **NO**. It is false about that carrier, and R2 didn't repair the carrier — it *replaced* it (`AffCoverData`, `Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCover.lean:145`, whose `cover : (⨆ j, pieces j) = ⊤` field is literally the joint covering this leaf wanted, with no chart typing). So R2 granted the leaf's wish on a different object rather than removing the leaf's obstruction.

**leak-image — REJECTED-AS: superseded (route a) + dead-route (route b)** · cause cited: route (a) *is* chart-avoid via `isClosed_supportLocus_inter_chart_of_forall_noLeak`; route (b) dead because a finer cover imposes more closed-trace constraints on the same fixed union · cause still holds: **YES** — the lemma is at `Picard/DivSchemeCertZarChartTrace.lean:129`, and the fixed-union fact is `supportLocus_inter_chart₀_eq_iUnion` (`:80`), whose `⊇` direction uses `Scheme.basicOpen_le`, i.e. it *needs* pieces to be basic opens of the chart · re-openable: **NO** as stated, but note the whole file's argument is chart-pair-only and cannot be restated over `AffCoverData`.

**tube-fibre — REJECTED-AS: superseded, and the supersession has since inverted** · cause cited: the goal was refuted by `not_exists_unique_support_piece`, and its reformulation is equivalent to chart-trace closedness · cause still holds: **YES textually, NO in force**. This is the finding I'd act on. The leaf's title objective is "put the family support … inside a single adaptation piece". That is verbatim `AffCoverData.SwallowedBy` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffSwallow.lean:75`), which R2 not only defines but **produces** — `exists_affCoverData_swallowedBy` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffStraddle.lean:95`) builds it from the 0B8B input, and the entire straddling capstone `isCertified_of_swallowedBy_of_c1` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffGlue.lean:318`) runs on it. Meanwhile the refutation cannot follow: `not_exists_unique_support_piece` (`Picard/DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean:257`) delegates to `supportLocus_disjoint_chart_inter_of_separated`, whose proof reads `A.toFinCoverData.cover₀`/`cover₁` at `:208-209` — the two chart-wise partitions. Nothing in it survives to `AffCoverData`. · re-openable: **NO — it is DONE, not open**. A rejected leaf's goal is a landed theorem on the live carrier. Marking it `rejected` is not wrong per se but it hides a granted objective.

**cert-relocalize — REJECTED-AS: false-statement (in-place refactor), with a now-dead prescription** · cause cited: `IsLocallyCertified`, `DivFamZar`, theta windows, cocycle, evaluation, `DivRepGlobalData.equiv` all fixed in one `pi`, so one classifier cannot classify the union over `M` · cause still holds: **YES** for the chart-typed side — `DivRepGlobalData` (`Picard/DivRepKit.lean:68`) has every field over `divFamZar C pi g`, and `DivOver` is a `pi`-dependent notation. · re-openable: **NO for the in-place refactor; YES for its residue, on the R2 carrier**. The residue "a fixed-pi classifier cannot internalize coordinate twists" is answered by the carrier being *pi-free*: `IsLocallyCertifiedAff` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffZar.lean:103`), `DivFamZarAff` (`:165`) and `divFunctorAff` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffMap.lean:290`) take `(C, R, n)` and no `pi` at all. The twist quantifier disappears rather than moving outward. **The row's forwarding sentence is stale at HEAD**: `cert-relocalize.yaml` line 14 still reads "Those obligations are tracked by twist-atlas", and twist-atlas is now rejected — a rejected leaf pointing at a rejected leaf, and that pointer is the only prescription it offers.

**twist-atlas — REJECTED-AS: forbidden (human decision), not false and not dead** · cause cited: instantiates at `twistedP1Map pi M`, which is the GL₂(k) action protection I-0492 clause 1 bars · cause still holds: **YES** — `twistedP1Map` is `π ≫ P1.autOfMatrix k M` at `Cohomology/TwistedFiberTwoCover.lean:29`, and `P1.autOfMatrix` at `Curve/P1Aut.lean:227` is docstring'd "**The GL₂(k)-twist of the projective line**". Both files are rooted (`AlgebraicJacobian.lean:7`, `:202`), so the action is *already built* — clause 1 bars consumers, not the existing file. · re-openable: **NO without a fresh human decision**. Answering (c) explicitly: twist-atlas is **not** part of the "one obstruction found three ways" group. That group is joint-cover / leak-image / tube-fibre, all about *where pieces live*; twist-atlas is about the *classifier*, and it is cert-relocalize's forwarding address. The parent's own text says so ("plus cert-relocalize, which is about the CLASSIFIER rather than the pieces") while omitting twist-atlas from the count entirely.

**away-kerspan — BLOCKED, correctly, and its fallback pointer is factually wrong** · Its own content checks out: `ovlColengthDiagEquiv` (`AffGlue:243`), `rankAtStalk_glued_eq_of_swallowedBy` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffRank.lean:88`), `deltaSub_apply_diag` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffCollapse.lean:84`), `affAdaptation_fibre_regular` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffFibre.lean:277`), `exists_affAdaptation_of_isProper` (`Picard/DivisorFamilyAffExtraction.lean:140`) all exist. Its general-case escape sentence does not: it says "ddr.flattening-fallback was rejected 2026-07-23 with an EMPTY note", but that row is **pending/low** and its summary opens "REJECTION REOPENED (2026-07-25, run 0048) — the recorded rejection rationale was checked and is factually wrong". That row's own cheapest experiment is still unrun: `AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/EntryIdeal.lean` is on disk (29514 bytes), imported by zero files, absent from `AlgebraicJacobian.lean` — the one-line rooting it asks for has never been done.

## Answers to (a) and (b)

(a) The obstruction is **pieces confined to the preimages of a fixed pair of P¹ points**, i.e. the chart-wise partitions of unity. The parent states it as: *"joint-cover, leak-image and tube-fibre are all symptoms of PIECES CONFINED TO A FIXED CHART PAIR, which is precisely what R2 removes."* I-0492 clause 5 gives the sharp form: *"NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of P1 can work."*

(b) R2 removed it, and this makes **none of the three re-openable as stated** — because R2 replaced the carrier rather than repairing it, and each rejection's ground is a fact *about the old carrier* that is still true of it. The free value is not a reopening: it is that tube-fibre's objective is already a landed, produced definition on the new carrier, and nothing on the board says so.

## Should the parent be restated?

Yes, but narrowly — the *formulation* is sound and the mathematics needs no restatement. Four textual fixes, all board-only:

1. Parent: "Four rejections and one block" → five, with twist-atlas named as the **classifier** branch (cert-relocalize's forwarding address), not a fourth piece-side dead end.
2. Parent + cert-relocalize: replace "Those obligations are tracked by twist-atlas" with the R2 pointer, citing the pi-freeness of `DivFamZarAff`/`divFunctorAff` as the *reason* the twist quantifier vanishes. The live descendants are `…ddr.divrep.framecover-aff` (owner `ajcr-p1`) and `…fieldmono-aff` (owner `ajcr-p3`).
3. tube-fibre: add one line saying its objective is `AffCoverData.SwallowedBy` and is produced by `exists_affCoverData_swallowedBy` — so a lane reading "rejected" doesn't conclude the containment is unavailable.
4. away-kerspan: correct the flattening sentence to flattening-fallback's actual status (pending/low, rejection reopened), and note the `EntryIdeal.lean` rooting is still unexecuted.

One more, outside the cluster but the same defect: `…certificate.finite-field-avoid.descent` had its priority dropped high→low, but its **summary was never edited** — it still prescribes "transport P1 automorphisms and fixed-twist divisor charts … semilinear Galois descent data … depends on the twist-atlas architecture". It is `pending`, hence claimable, and the priority change is invisible to a lane reading the text.

Files that matter: `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.certificate.yaml` and its `.cert-relocalize` / `.tube-fibre` / `.away-kerspan` / `.finite-field-avoid.descent` siblings; `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/.archon-horizon/roadmap/items/AJCR.w4-rep.datum.dat-d.ddr.flattening-fallback.yaml`; `/home/axel/LeanAlgebraicGeometry-Horizon/MainProjects/Algebraic-Jacobian-Challenge-Rebuild/AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivisorFamilyAffSwallow.lean`, `…/DivisorFamilyAffStraddle.lean`, `…/DivSchemeCertZarSep.lean`, `…/DivisorFamilyAffZar.lean`, `…/Picard/EntryIdeal.lean`.

I read the roadmap and Lean only; no edits, no `lake build`. All roadmap facts were read at HEAD via `git show` (the parent and twist-atlas yaml also hash-match disk), so the I-0889 revert hazard is not in play for what I quoted.
